theory.intro: **Equivalent fractions** name the same amount in different ways, such as $\tfrac{6}{8} = \tfrac{3}{4}$. They shade the same area and sit at the same point on a number line.
facts: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the same whole number greater than $0$ to split the parts equally. To group parts, divide both by the same number, with no remainder.
Grouping or splitting equal parts changes their number and size, but keeps the same amount of the whole.
steps: To split each part equally, multiply the numerator and denominator by the same number.
To group equal parts, divide the numerator and denominator by the same number, with no remainder.
When the requested denominator needs both steps, group first, then split. Check that the amount stays the same.

workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $5\times4=20$, so multiply both parts by $4$.
$\frac{3}{5}=\frac{3\times4}{5\times4}=\frac{12}{20}$
The missing numerator is $12$.
(b) $7\times2=14$, so multiply both parts by $2$.
$\frac{7}{8}=\frac{7\times2}{8\times2}=\frac{14}{16}$
The missing denominator is $16$.

(a) $10$ of the $15$ equal parts are shaded: $\frac{10}{15}$.
(b) Each group contains $5$ small parts.
$\frac{10}{15}=\frac{10\div5}{15\div5}=\frac{2}{3}$
Both bars have the same whole and the same shaded amount.

workedExamples.question_text:
Complete $\frac{10}{16}=\frac{\square}{24}$.
First group the sixteenths into eighths, then split the eighths into twenty-fourths.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Group $2$ small parts together.
$\frac{10}{16}=\frac{10\div2}{16\div2}=\frac{5}{8}$
Split each eighth into $3$ equal parts.
$\frac{5}{8}=\frac{5\times3}{8\times3}=\frac{15}{24}$
The missing numerator is $15$.
